_about: My review (manual) of the automated underspecified variants of Phase 2's calibration, against my hand-made Phase 1 variants. valid: the request with the seed is a correct underspecified test (the intended records, and only they, fully meet a request that refers to one specific record). natural: a real user could write it. faithful: only the dropped condition was removed (rules 1, 2 and 5 of the writer). Written 2026-09-27 at 00:07, after reading every accepted variant of cal1 (34 of 37 records; 3 still running then).

U-BOX-21-Folder_created_at.note: Changed 'Leo Park last modified' to 'last modified by Leo Park' (unasked, but it removes the superlative reading the readers raised).

U-BOX-22-HubItem_file.note: 'the hub updated by Dana Whitfield' drops 'last' (and the final period). The seed stores only the last updater, so the match set is the same; the wording is looser than the condition.

U-BOX-23-File_comment_count.note: ', that is larger than 2 MB' where I wrote 'and that is'; slightly stiff.

U-BOX-24-Task_created_at.note: 'the task pat.kim@... asking to check' reads better than mine ('... created asking to check'), which is awkward.

U-CAL-21-Event_description.note: 'the event with planning in the title' replaces 'the planning session' to make the freed 'Q4 roadmap planning' fit; a test-like phrase. The added-words check (added after cal1) flags it.

U-CAL-23-EventAttendee_email.note: Adds 'on June 22' (redundant with Friday) and 'someone'. The added-words check flags it.

U-LIN-24-Cycle_number.note: 'into a cycle of the Engineering team' is indefinite: any cycle fits, so picking one is correct and the test is not underspecified. Mine: 'the Engineering team's cycle'. Led to the definite-reference rule for the writer and the reader.

U-LIN-22-Document_projectId.note: 'the doc whose last edit was by Leo Park' for 'the doc Leo Park last edited': the same unasked disambiguation of the superlative reading as in BOX-21 (read at 00:09).

cal1_dropf_summary: 37 facts; 31 derivable by code (my call on 37 of 37); 27 accepted, 3 declined by the writer, 1 rejected after three rounds. Of the 27 accepted: 17 identical to mine, 4 equivalent, 6 reworded beyond the dropped condition (3 of them disambiguate 'X last modified/updated/edited'); 25 of 27 valid and natural (LIN-24 is indefinite, CAL-21's is test-like). The added-words check, applied after the fact, flags 2 of 27 (CAL-21 description, CAL-23 email).

cal3_dropf._read: 2026-09-27 01:07, all 23 accepted variants of iteration 3 (the calibration of record) against mine.

U-BOX-23-File_comment_count.note: ', that is larger than 2 MB' for 'and that is'.

U-LIN-24-Cycle_number.note: 'into that cycle of the Engineering team': definite, but 'that' points at nothing said before; unnatural.

cal3_dropf.summary: 23 of 31 derivable facts accepted (cal1: 27); 20 identical to mine, 2 equivalent, 1 unnatural: 22 of 23 valid and natural (96%). Declined 4 (the tied 'last updated'; 'contract' twice; 'the planning session' read as an exact title) and rejected 4 by the reader (two for the scenario's own wording, 'includes a file', and the ambiguity of 'Friday's' on a Sunday, which is fact_coverage_02's).

cal1_dropf_not_accepted.U-BOX-22-File_name: Declined: the writer holds that 'Dana Whitfield last updated' becomes superlative-ambiguous once the file's name is gone. A fair concern about fact_coverage_02's wording, not a failure of the writer.
cal1_dropf_not_accepted.U-BOX-23-File_description: Declined: the writer reads 'contract' as a condition that excludes the freed near miss (8102, 'Master terms, signed 2024'); I think 8102 is a contract, so this decline is too cautious.
cal1_dropf_not_accepted.U-BOX-23-File_extension: Declined: 'contract' would exclude the freed 'Initech pricing.docx'. A fair point: my hand-made 'the contract file ...' may not make 8105 a match for a careful reader. Watched in the labels.
cal1_dropf_not_accepted.U-CAL-23-EventAttendee_optional: Rejected after three rounds: the writer kept adding disambiguation ('in the title', the date) and the reader found it unnatural.
